entries.title: Moving along at their own pace
entries.summary: Davies describes a low trike or balance bike moved along with the feet, with a pedal tricycle as a separate, later possibility. Interest and what the child can manage guide the choice.
entries.cue: Your child is interested in riding and a different way of moving may be appealing.
detail: Her appendix groups foot-propelled riding at 14–16 months. The photographed balance-bike example has a different label: from around 2 years, once the child is tall enough. Those are separate presentations, not a deadline to combine.

In the balance-bike example, the child pushes with their feet and gradually explores coasting at their own pace. Davies describes a later move to a regular bike as something that often happens, not a promised result.
The appendix introduces pedal tricycles from 2½ years. Pedaling is a different movement from pushing along with the feet; an age label does not replace watching what the child can manage.
Riding is one of many movement possibilities alongside running, dancing and ball play. The examples are not a collection every family needs to buy.
